label: <DEL> step of sequences beginning with two binary digits (0/1)
explanation: Very sparse feature (~195 activations in 1M sequences), firing only at the delimiter step (t == L, recall_idx 0). All activations are in sequences whose first original token is 0 or 1, and ~87% (89% of mass) also have 0 or 1 as the second token; the 0 then 1 pattern dominates (out_tok 0 = 77% of mass, next_out 1 = 67%). Mostly fires for L = 6-8; never L <= 4, rarely L = 9; more digits in the sequence raises the rate. It never fires in the original or copy phases, or when the sequence starts with a letter. Precision is low (~4%): only a small fraction of <DEL> steps with a binary-digit opening fire, and adding L or last-token conditions did not find what decides which ones fire. Magnitude claims beyond the dominant 0,1 opening were not checked.
